author.bio: Thomas Szasz (1920–2012) was a Hungarian-American psychiatrist and longtime professor at SUNY Upstate Medical University. Known for The Myth of Mental Illness, he challenged coercion and the use of psychiatric language as social control; The Second Sin presents his observations in aphoristic form.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: In The Second Sin, Szasz arranges short judgments under topical headings rather than building a continuous narrative. The boredom-and-serenity contrast is cited to the section “Emotions,” where nearby aphorisms also examine happiness, anxiety and courage. Its mirrored syntax makes the change in outlook, rather than a change in available time, the focus.
